title: Open question on twin-width over infinite fields
statement_text: An intriguing question concerns the existence of such results (almost linear-time multiplication of matrices of bounded twin-width given by twin-decompositions, known over finite fields) over infinite fields (starting with $\mathbb{Q}$). We do not have a direct definition of twin-width of matrices over $\mathbb{Q}$ based on contraction sequences. However linear-minor freeness naturally carries to infinite fields, and thus, it is natural to consider that a class of matrices over $\mathbb{Q}$ has bounded twin-width if its closure under linear minors is not the set of all matrices. This can be equivalently stated via the notion of grid rank of a matrix $M$, i.e., the largest $k$ for which there is a $k\times k$ subdivision of $M$ in which every block has rank at least $k$. We believe that computing the product of two matrices over $\mathbb{Q}$ with bounded grid rank should be done in almost quadratic time, however, we lack a structural decomposition as in the finite field case.
context_text: Matrices have ordered rows and columns, and a matrix class is a set of matrices closed under taking submatrices. A linear minor of a matrix $M$ over a field is a matrix obtained by a succession of replacements of two consecutive rows, or two consecutive columns, by a linear combination of them; equivalently, one partitions the columns into intervals and picks one column vector in the span of each part, then does the same with the rows (over $\mathbb{F}_2$ this amounts to deletions and sums of consecutive rows or columns, called parity minors). A class excludes $M$ as a linear minor if $M$ is not a linear minor of any matrix of the class; a $k\times k$ subdivision (or $k$-division) partitions the rows and the columns into $k$ intervals each. Over a finite field, twin-width of matrices is defined by contraction sequences, and the authors prove that a matrix class over a finite field has bounded twin-width if and only if it excludes some matrix as a linear minor. They also give an algorithm that, given two $n\times n$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_q$ as twin-decompositions (a compact tree-based representation derived from contraction sequences) of width at most $d$, computes a twin-decomposition of their product in time $q^{2d+o(d)}n$, with entries then queryable in time $O(1/\varepsilon)$ after $2^{O_q(d)}n^{1+\varepsilon}$ preprocessing. The question is whether analogous results hold over infinite fields. The authors note that a linear minor of a matrix of grid rank $k$ has grid rank at most $k$, and that a class has bounded grid rank if and only if it excludes some matrix as a linear minor.
